note: Each stop names a sentence that is already in a cleaned public-domain book on this shelf. The page shows the whole passage that contains that sentence. The guide is a note from the room, not a quotation.

paths.title: A city, and the person in it
paths.blurb: Five stops in the books already on the ancient table: justice, the city, duty, what is in our power, and the society of other people.

stops.needle: But then, I said, speaking the truth and paying your debts is not a correct definition of justice.
stops.ask: Is paying what you owe a sufficient account of justice in a city?
stops.guide: The Republic’s first book tries a definition of justice and sets it aside. The path starts at that refusal.

stops.needle: What is a city?
stops.ask: What makes a city a city, rather than a crowd living under a government?
stops.guide: Aristotle’s Politics asks what a city is before it sorts the forms of government.

stops.needle: I should like at the outset to define what duty is
stops.ask: Can a rule of duty stand if moral goodness is not worth seeking for its own sake?
stops.guide: Cicero tells his son that a discussion of duty has to begin by saying what duty is.

stops.needle: Demand not that events should happen as you wish
stops.ask: Should a person demand that events happen as he wishes?
stops.guide: The Enchiridion separates what is in a person’s power from what is not.

stops.needle: if there be any gods, it is no grievous thing to leave the society of men
stops.ask: What does a person owe other people, if death ends that society?
stops.guide: Marcus writes to himself about death and the society of men in the same breath.

paths.title: Rest, imitation, and the heart
paths.blurb: Four stops in the Christian books on this shelf: the Confessions, the Imitation, the Consolation, and the Pensées.

stops.needle: our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee
stops.ask: What is a heart for, if it is restless until it rests in God?
stops.guide: The Confessions open on praise and on a heart that does not sit still.

stops.needle: What doth it profit thee to enter into deep discussion concerning the Holy Trinity
stops.ask: Does knowing the arguments matter if the life does not follow?
stops.guide: The Imitation sets a holy life beside skill in definitions.

stops.needle: I brought to my duties no aim but zeal for the public good
stops.ask: Is public office justified by zeal for the public good?
stops.guide: In the Consolation, Boethius answers the charge against his public life.

stops.needle: The heart has its reasons, which reason does not know
stops.loc: Preface to the second part.--To speak of those who have treated of this matter., paragraph 48
stops.ask: What can people share if the heart has reasons that argument does not reach?
stops.guide: Pascal distinguishes the heart’s order from the order of demonstration.

paths.title: Learning, profit, and the way
paths.blurb: Five stops, one in each school’s book on this table. The schools are not collapsed into one doctrine.

stops.needle: Is it not pleasant to learn with a constant perseverance and application?
stops.ask: What does learning ask of a person who may go unnoticed?
stops.guide: The Analects begin with learning, friends, and the person who is not thrown off when others take no notice.

stops.needle: Why must your Majesty used that word 'profit'?
stops.ask: Should a ruler ask first how to profit the kingdom?
stops.guide: Mencius’s first exchange with King Hui is about profit, benevolence, and righteousness. The English is Legge’s, including his wording.

stops.needle: The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao
stops.ask: Can the way a people walk be named and still be the enduring way?
stops.guide: The Tao Teh King opens by distinguishing the way that can be walked and named from the enduring way.

stops.needle: In the northern ocean there is a fish, called the Leviathan
stops.ask: What is the use of a greatness that does not fit an ordinary measure?
stops.guide: Giles’s Chuang Tzu opens on a fish that becomes a bird too large for an ordinary sky.

stops.needle: in those who harbour such thoughts hatred will never cease
stops.ask: Does holding an injury keep hatred alive among people?
stops.guide: The Twin-Verses of the Dhammapada set harbouring an injury next to letting it go.

paths.title: Law, liberty, and the moral law
paths.blurb: Four stops in the Enlightenment books on this shelf: Hume, Rousseau, Wollstonecraft, and Kant.

stops.needle: Good laws may beget order and moderation in the government
stops.loc: THAT POLITICS MAY BE REDUCED TO A SCIENCE, paragraph 66
stops.ask: Can good laws produce moderation where manners have not?
stops.guide: Hume’s essay on politics as a science weighs laws against manners.

stops.needle: all, being born free and equal, alienate their liberty only for their own advantage
stops.ask: If people are born free and equal, why would they give liberty up?
stops.guide: The Social Contract’s chapter on first societies compares the family with the state.

stops.needle: considering females rather as women than human creatures
stops.work: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
stops.ask: What education is owed to women if they are rational creatures?
stops.guide: Wollstonecraft’s introduction objects to an education that aims at allurement rather than reason.

stops.needle: the moral law is the condition under which we can first become conscious of freedom
stops.ask: Is the moral law the way a person becomes aware of freedom?
stops.guide: Kant’s preface ties the moral law to the awareness of freedom.

paths.title: Society, faction, and union
paths.blurb: Four stops in the founding books on this shelf: Common Sense, Federalist 10, The Way to Wealth, and the Farewell Address.

stops.needle: Some writers have so confounded society with government
stops.loc: Of the origin and design of government, paragraph 1
stops.ask: Are society and government the same thing, or do they begin from different needs?
stops.guide: Common Sense opens by separating society from government.

stops.needle: By a faction, I understand a number of citizens
stops.ask: How should a republic deal with a faction that shares a passion?
stops.guide: This edition labels Federalist 10 as Madison’s. The path uses that paper’s definition of faction.

stops.needle: early to bed, and early to rise, makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise
stops.ask: Does a shared counsel of work and thrift hold a people together?
stops.guide: The Way to Wealth is Father Abraham repeating Poor Richard. The sentence is inside that speech.

stops.needle: exhibit the continuance of the union as a primary object of patriotic desire
stops.ask: Why would a union be the first object of a patriot’s care?
stops.guide: The Farewell Address treats the continuance of the union as a primary public object.
